lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 92, which adds the -t and -T options to open folders as tabs in one new window.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request 92, which adds the dash t and dash capital T options to open folders as tabs in one new window.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You run thunar with -t and some folders, then -T and more folders.
lines.say: You run Thunar with dash t and some folders, then dash capital T and more folders.

lines.caption: Still in your own process, the command splits its arguments at -T, and marks the right-pane folders.
lines.say: Still in your own process, the command splits its arguments at dash capital T, and marks the right-pane folders.

lines.caption: Then GApplication hands the options to the Thunar that is already running, over D-Bus.
lines.say: Then G Application hands the options to the Thunar that is already running, over D bus.

lines.caption: That Thunar reads the new options, and the list of right-pane folders.
It checks each folder; a bad one gets the error dialog and exit status 1. The rest are then checked one at a time.
lines.say: It checks each folder; a bad one gets the error dialog and exit status one. The rest are then checked one at a time.

lines.caption: It always opens a new window, as with -w, and skips restoring last session's tabs.
lines.say: It always opens a new window, as with dash w, and skips restoring last session's tabs.

lines.caption: A new window function fills the left pane, turns split view on only with -T, and fills the right pane.
lines.say: A new window function fills the left pane, turns split view on only with dash capital T, and fills the right pane.

lines.caption: Finally the first tab is selected in each pane, and the keyboard focus goes back to the left pane.
Until now each folder opened in its own window; there was no way to build a two-pane window of tabs in one command.
The key fact: the thunar you type usually just forwards its options to a running Thunar, so the split must happen first.
lines.say: The key fact: the Thunar you type usually just forwards its options to a running Thunar, so the split must happen first.

lines.caption: The split also finds -T inside combined flags like -tT; -T with no folder exits with an error, unless help or version is asked for.
lines.say: The split also finds dash capital T inside combined flags, like dash t capital T; dash capital T with no folder exits with an error, unless help or version is asked for.

lines.caption: Bulk rename with -t or -T is refused here too, so no Thunar starts just to print the error.
lines.say: Bulk rename with dash t or dash capital T is refused here too, so no Thunar starts just to print the error.

lines.caption: Every name is checked while your command waits; missing ones, files and names with no working folder exit with status 1.
lines.say: Every name is checked while your command waits; missing ones, files and names with no working folder exit with status one.

lines.caption: Every location that needs a check waits in one queue, so two mounts or password prompts never run at once.
The trade-off: remote tabs that are already mounted open a little slower, because they wait their turn too.
With nothing before -T, or when every left folder fails, the left pane gets the folder you ran the command in.
lines.say: With nothing before dash capital T, or when every left folder fails, the left pane gets the folder you ran the command in.

lines.caption: The window is new even when Open new windows as tabs is on.
The right pane now opens straight on its own folder; with -t alone, split view is turned off, even if always enabled.
lines.say: The right pane now opens straight on its own folder; with dash t alone, split view is turned off, even if always enabled.

lines.caption: Thunar normally selects the last tab opened, so the first tab is selected on purpose.
This table sums it up: -t a b -T c d fills both panes; -t a b fills only the left pane.
lines.say: This table sums it up: with both options, both panes fill; with dash t alone, only the left pane.

lines.caption: -T c alone puts the current folder on the left; -T with nothing after it is an error, exits with status 1, and opens no window.
lines.say: Dash capital T with one folder puts the current folder on the left; dash capital T with nothing after it is an error, exits with status one, and opens no window.

lines.caption: Bulk rename with -t or -T is an error too: it exits with status 1 and opens nothing.
lines.say: Bulk rename with dash t or dash capital T is an error too: it exits with status one and opens nothing.

lines.caption: A missing folder gets the usual dialog and exit status 1, then the rest open; without these options nothing changes.
lines.say: A missing folder gets the usual dialog and exit status one, then the rest open; without these options nothing changes.

lines.caption: If the left folders all fail, the left pane gets the current folder; a remote sftp folder is mounted first, and a failed mount just shows the dialog.
lines.say: If the left folders all fail, the left pane gets the current folder; a remote S F T P folder is mounted first, and a failed mount just shows the dialog.

lines.caption: A side effect: Thunar now passes on its exit status, so usage errors and missing folders exit with 1 instead of 0.
lines.say: A side effect: Thunar now passes on its exit status, so usage errors and missing folders exit with one instead of zero.

lines.caption: The PR changes seven Thunar source files and adds a test, this page and its narration. Bulk rename with -t or -T is now refused.
lines.say: The PR changes seven Thunar source files and adds a test, this page and its narration. Bulk rename with dash t or dash capital T is now refused.

lines.caption: One change reaches beyond tabs: the shared mount helper now tells every caller the real reason a location failed after mounting.
To undo it, revert this PR; nothing is stored in settings.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows issue 4's table, reuses Thunar's own new-window path, and Thunar's usual error dialog.
In this session's local run, not CI, an earlier head built with no gcc warnings, and all 10 tests passed.
lines.say: In this session's local run, not C I, an earlier head built with no G C C warnings, and all ten tests passed.

lines.caption: The new test ran the issue's example with no Thunar running, and stepped through both panes' tabs.
With Thunar running and new windows as tabs on, it still opened new windows, with and without the right pane.
The current folder filled the left pane; -T alone printed its error, opened nothing and exited with status 1.
lines.say: The current folder filled the left pane; dash capital T alone printed its error, opened nothing and exited with status one.

lines.caption: A missing folder got the error dialog and the rest opened, help lists both options, and the test took 18 seconds.
lines.say: A missing folder got the error dialog and the rest opened, help lists both options, and the test took eighteen seconds.

lines.caption: Not run: a file that isn't a folder, a remote location, and the mount queue.
A local audit by the shot-auditor agent passed all 9 screenshots, taken on an earlier build.
lines.say: A local audit by the shot auditor agent passed all nine screenshots, taken on an earlier build.

lines.caption: Auditing CI's screenshots of the final head is still to come.
lines.say: Auditing C I's screenshots of the final head is still to come.

lines.caption: An earlier CI verify run passed its tests, then failed only at uploading its files, a CI problem, not this change.
lines.say: An earlier C I verify run passed its tests, then failed only at uploading its files, a C I problem, not this change.

lines.caption: The test now also checks that bulk rename with -t is refused; CI's result is still to come.
lines.say: The test now also checks that bulk rename with dash t is refused; C I's result is still to come.

lines.caption: On an earlier head CI built, passed all 10 tests and its review; CI's run on the latest head is still to come.
lines.say: On an earlier head C I built, passed all ten tests and its review; C I's run on the latest head is still to come.

lines.caption: A fresh review agent looked six times, and fixed most of what it found; the rest was kept on purpose. Its last two looks found nothing.
Three were in the test script, and two in messages, like help with -T showing the error instead.
lines.say: Three were in the test script, and two in messages, like help with dash capital T showing the error instead.

lines.caption: Kept: -t alone turns split view off, because the issue asks for the left pane only.
lines.say: Kept: dash t alone turns split view off, because the issue asks for the left pane only.

lines.caption: The second review's fixes keep right-pane tabs when the left ones fail, and exit 1 on a failed folder; two things were kept.
lines.say: The second review's fixes keep right-pane tabs when the left ones fail, and exit with one on a failed folder; two things were kept.

lines.caption: The third look found four bugs, like a location vanishing while mounting, and all four were fixed.
The fourth look found that parallel checks could mount one volume twice, so unmounted locations now queue.
CI's own review, at level high, has looked at the PR nine times, with 70 findings, R1 to R70.
lines.say: C I's own review, at level high, has looked at the PR nine times, with seventy findings, R 1 to R 70.

lines.caption: The first ten covered the split at -T, mounting, the exit status and the right pane, and all were fixed.
lines.say: The first ten covered the split at dash capital T, mounting, the exit status and the right pane, and all were fixed.

lines.caption: CI fixed the second round itself; this session fixed the third, by checking every location in the handler.
lines.say: C I fixed the second round itself; this session fixed the third, by checking every location in the handler.

lines.caption: CI fixed six of the fourth round itself, moving the vanishing-location fix into the shared mount helper.
lines.say: C I fixed six of the fourth round itself, moving the vanishing location fix into the shared mount helper.

lines.caption: The last three, all low and unconfirmed, were accepted: one can't happen, one is deliberate, one keeps the code simple.
In the fifth round, the always-not-found error and the one-by-one checks of mounted remote locations were fixed.
lines.say: In the fifth round, the always not found error and the one by one checks of mounted remote locations were fixed.

lines.caption: Its other five, all low and unconfirmed, were left as they are; most describe intended behaviour.
The sixth round's three fixes put shortcuts and mountables in the queue too, and tidied the code.
Its other five were accepted: most match plain thunar or lie outside this issue.
lines.say: Its other five were accepted: most match plain Thunar or lie outside this issue.

lines.caption: The seventh round found a stale mounted flag, a doubled queue test, and a mountable with no target; all are fixed.
The seventh round's other five were accepted: one under the owner's decision next, four as minor and unconfirmed.
CI kept trading speed against safety for mounted remote tabs, so the owner chose: everything goes one at a time.
lines.say: C I kept trading speed against safety for mounted remote tabs, so the owner chose: everything goes one at a time.

lines.caption: The eighth round came after main was merged in. CI fixed one finding itself: bulk rename with -t or -T now gives an error.
lines.say: The eighth round came after main was merged in. C I fixed one finding itself: bulk rename with dash t or dash capital T now gives an error.

lines.caption: It also noted that -t alone turns split view off; the owner kept that, since the issue asks for one pane.
lines.say: It also noted that dash t alone turns split view off; the owner kept that, since the issue asks for one pane.

lines.caption: Its other six were minor and unconfirmed, and were accepted as they are.
The ninth round's two fixes CI made itself: the bulk rename refusal now happens in your own process, and the test checks it.
lines.say: The ninth round's two fixes C I made itself: the bulk rename refusal now happens in your own process, and the test checks it.

lines.caption: Its other three were minor and unconfirmed, and were accepted as they are.
CI's run on the latest head is still to come, and so is the visual check of its screenshots.
lines.say: C I's run on the latest head is still to come, and so is the visual check of its screenshots.

The pull request, its checks and CI's comments are linked here.
lines.say: The pull request, its checks and C I's comments are linked here.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later: issue 41, a split option.
Issue 41 adds --split, which opens a new window with split view at a given percentage.
lines.say: Issue 41 adds a split option, which opens a new window with split view at a given percentage.

lines.caption: Whichever lands second makes -T windows open at that split, and -t alone open the right pane on the first tab.
lines.say: Whichever lands second makes these windows open at that split, and dash t alone open the right pane on the first tab.

lines.caption: Issue 41 is next: it adds the option, then wires it to this PR's tabs, as its own issue lists.
In short: one command now opens a new window with your chosen tabs in one or both panes, focus on the left.
